cues.en: Well, what happens is,
cues.zh: 事情通常是这样的，

cues.en: like with John Scully,
cues.zh: 就像 John Sculley 那样，

cues.en: John came from PepsiCo,
cues.zh: John 之前来自百事可乐，

cues.en: and they they at most would change their product, you know, once every ten years. I mean, to them a new product was like a new size bottle, Right?
cues.zh: 他们顶多也就是每十年才换一次产品。我是说，对他们而言，换个瓶子尺寸就算新产品了，对吧？

cues.en: So if you were a product person,
cues.zh: 所以如果你是个做产品的人，

cues.en: you couldn't change the course of that company very much. So who influenced the success of PepsiCo? The sales and marketing people. Therefore, they were the ones that got promoted, and therefore, they were the ones that ran the company.
cues.zh: 你根本没法对那家公司产生太大影响。那么是谁决定了百事可乐的成功？是销售和市场人员。因此，获得升迁的是他们，最终掌管公司的也是他们。

cues.en: Well,
cues.zh: 嗯，

cues.en: for PepsiCo that might have been okay,
cues.zh: 对百事公司来说，这也许还行，

cues.en: but
cues.zh: 但

cues.en: it turns out the same thing can happen in technology companies that get monopolies,
cues.zh: 事实证明，在形成垄断的科技公司里也会发生同样的事，

cues.en: like, oh, IBM and Xerox.
cues.zh: 比如 IBM 和施乐。

cues.en: If you were a product person at IBM or Xerox,
cues.zh: 如果你是 IBM 或施乐的产品人员，

cues.en: so you make a better copy or a better computer, so what? When you have a monopoly market share,
cues.zh: 你做出了更好的复印机或更好的电脑，那又怎样？当你拥有垄断市场份额时，

cues.en: the company is not any more successful.
cues.zh: 公司并不会因此更成功。

cues.en: So the people that can make the company more successful are sales and marketing people,
cues.zh: 所以能让公司更成功的是销售和营销人员，

cues.en: and they end up running the companies.
cues.zh: 最终他们掌管了公司。

cues.en: And the product people get driven out of decision making forums.
cues.zh: 产品人员被排挤出决策会议。

cues.en: And the companies forget
cues.zh: 公司也忘了

cues.en: what it means to make great products.
cues.zh: 怎样才能做出优秀的产品。

cues.en: It sort of the product
cues.zh: 产品的那种

cues.en: sensibility
cues.zh: 敏锐度

cues.en: and the product genius that brought them to that monopolistic position gets rotted out
cues.zh: 以及让它们取得垄断地位的产品天赋，都被这些公司的管理者一点点磨掉了。

cues.en: by people running these companies who have no conception
cues.zh: 他们根本不懂

cues.en: of a good product versus a bad product. They have no conception of the craftsmanship
cues.zh: 什么是好产品，什么是坏产品。他们也不懂，把一个好点子变成好产品需要怎样的匠心。

cues.en: that's required to take a good idea and turn it into a good product. And they really have no feeling in their hearts usually about wanting to really help the customers.
cues.zh: 而且通常，他们心里也没有真正帮助客户的意愿。

cues.en: So that's what happened at Xerox. The the people at Xerox PARC used to call the people that ran Xerox toner heads.
cues.zh: 这就是当年在 Xerox 发生的事。Xerox PARC 的人过去常把 Xerox 的管理层叫做“碳粉脑壳”。

cues.en: And they just had... And these toner heads would come out to Xerox PARC and they just had no clue about what they were seeing. And for our our audience, toner is what? Oh, toner. Toner is what you put into a copier.
cues.zh: 他们根本……而这些“碳粉脑壳”来到 Xerox PARC，完全看不懂自己眼前看到的一切。给我们的观众解释一下，碳粉是指什么？哦，碳粉。碳粉就是你加进复印机里的东西。

cues.en: Yeah. You know, the toner that you add to a... To an industrial copier. The black stuff. The black stuff. Yeah. So they basically they were copier heads. They just had no clue about
cues.zh: 对。就是你加进……加进工业复印机里的碳粉。黑乎乎的那种。黑乎乎的那种粉末。没错。所以他们本质上就是一群“复印机脑壳”。他们对计算机

cues.en: computer or what it could do. And so they they just grabbed
cues.zh: 或者计算机能做什么一无所知。所以他们就硬生生

cues.en: grabbed defeat from the greatest victory in the computer industry.
cues.zh: 把计算机行业最伟大的胜利拱手送成了惨败。

cues.en: Xerox could have owned the entire computer industry today.
cues.zh: 施乐本可以拥有今天的整个计算机产业。

cues.en: Could have been, you know, a company 10 times its size. Could have been IBM.
cues.zh: 本可以成为一家规模十倍于此的公司。本可以成为IBM。

cues.en: Could have been the IBM of the nineties. Could have been the Microsoft of the nineties.
cues.zh: 本可以成为九十年代的IBM。本可以成为九十年代的微软。

cues.en: So...
cues.zh: 所以……

cues.en: But anyway, that's all ancient history. It doesn't really matter anymore. Sure.
cues.zh: 但不管怎样，那都是陈年旧事了。现在已经无所谓了。当然。
